◆ addDefaultConstructorIfRequired()

SageInterface::addDefaultConstructorIfRequired ( SgClassType *  classType,
int  physical_file_id = Sg_File_Info::TRANSFORMATION_FILE_ID 
)

Adds a default constructor to a class if it does not have one but has other constructors.

This function checks if a given SgClassType has any constructors. If at least one constructor is found, it then checks for the presence of a default constructor (i.e., a constructor with no parameters). If a default constructor is not found, this function generates and adds a default constructor to the class. This is necessary because the compiler will not generate a default constructor if any other constructors are present.

Parameters
classTypeThe SgClassType that may need a default constructor added. Must be non-null.
physical_file_idThe file ID associated with the code being modified. Defaults to -1.
Returns
True if a default constructor was successfully added, false otherwise.

The updated mangled name is then stored in the cache for future reference.

◆ annotateExpressionsWithUniqueNames()

void SageInterface::annotateExpressionsWithUniqueNames ( SgProject *  project)

Annotates expressions in an AST with unique names.

This function traverses the abstract syntax tree (AST) of a given SgProject and annotates each expression node with a unique name. The unique name is generated based on the expression's class name and other factors to ensure uniqueness within the project.

Parameters
projectA pointer to an SgProject object representing the AST to be annotated.
Returns
None
Warning
This function modifies the input AST by adding new attributes to expression nodes. It does not perform any checks for existing annotations or handle potential naming conflicts.
Precondition
The input project must be a valid, non-null pointer to an SgProject object. The project's AST should be properly constructed and contain at least one expression node.
Postcondition
After executing this function, each expression node in the input project's AST will have a new attribute named "UniqueNameAttribute" containing a unique name generated based on the expression's class name.
Note
This function uses a recursive traversal approach to visit all nodes in the input AST. It assumes that the input project's AST is well-formed and does not contain any cycles or invalid node references.

Appends an expression to a list of expressions and sets the parent-child relationship.

This function takes a list of expressions (SgExprListExp) and an individual expression (SgExpression), appends the latter to the former, and establishes the parent-child relationship between them. The function relies on the ROSE library's assertion mechanism to ensure that both input arguments are valid.

Parameters
expListA pointer to a list of expressions. Must not be NULL.
expA pointer to an individual expression. Must not be NULL.
Returns
None (void)
Warning
This function does not perform any error handling beyond the assertions provided by ROSE_ASSERT. If either input argument is invalid, the program will terminate with an assertion failure.
Precondition
Both expList and exp must be non-NULL pointers to valid objects of their respective types.
Postcondition
The expression list (expList) has been modified to include the new expression (exp), and the parent-child relationship between them has been established. Specifically, expList is now a parent of exp in the abstract syntax tree (AST).
Note
This function does not create copies of either the input list or expression; it modifies the original objects.

void SageInterface::appendStatement ( SgStatement *  stmt,
SgForInitStatement *  for_init_stmt 
)

Appends a statement to the initialization list of a for loop.

This function appends a given statement to the initialization list of a for loop and updates internal data structures accordingly. It ensures that any macro expansions associated with the appended statement are properly recorded and marked as transformations.

The function takes two parameters: the statement to be appended and the for loop's initialization statement where the appending will occur. It performs several checks and updates before actually appending the statement, including checking if the statement is a moved statement and updating internal maps for both the target statement and its surrounding scope.

Parameters
stmtThe statement to be appended to the for loop's initialization list. Must not be NULL.
for_init_stmtThe for loop's initialization statement where the appending will occur. Must not be NULL.
Returns
None
Warning
This function does not perform any error handling if the input parameters are invalid. It assumes that the inputs are valid and will result in undefined behavior otherwise.
Precondition
The input parameters must not be NULL. The statement to be appended must be a valid SgStatement object, and the for loop's initialization statement must be a valid SgForInitStatement object.
Postcondition
The internal data structures are updated to reflect the appending of the statement. Any macro expansions associated with the appended statement are properly recorded and marked as transformations.
Note
This function is used internally by the SageInterface class and should not be called directly from outside the class.

Appends a list of statements to a given scope in the AST.

This function iterates over a vector of statements and appends each statement to the specified scope in the Abstract Syntax Tree (AST). It relies on the appendStatement() function to perform the actual appending, deferring the logic of checking parent pointers to that function.

None, as this function does not return any value. The result of the operation is reflected in the modified AST.

Precondition
The input vector of statements should not be empty. If it is, no operation will be performed. The specified scope should not be NULL, as this would lead to a segmentation fault.
Postcondition
After successful execution, the input statements will have been appended to the specified scope in the AST.
Note
This function does not perform any checks on the validity of the input statements or scope. It is the responsibility of the caller to ensure that these are valid and correctly set up.

◆ buildDeclarationSets()

SageInterface::DeclarationSets * SageInterface::buildDeclarationSets ( SgNode *  n)

Builds a set of declaration statements from an AST subtree.

This function constructs a collection of SgDeclarationStatement nodes by traversing the abstract syntax tree (AST) rooted at the given node. It uses a preorder traversal strategy to visit each node in the tree, and for each SgDeclarationStatement encountered, it adds the statement to the declaration set.

The function returns a pointer to the constructed DeclarationSets object, which contains all the SgDeclarationStatement nodes found in the AST subtree. This allows clients to iterate over the declarations and perform further analysis or processing as needed.

Parameters
nThe root node of the AST subtree from which to build the declaration sets. Must be a valid non-null pointer to an SgNode object.
Returns
A pointer to the constructed DeclarationSets object, containing all SgDeclarationStatement nodes found in the AST subtree. Returns nullptr if the input node is null or if no declarations are found in the tree.
Warning
The function does not perform any semantic analysis on the declarations; it simply collects them based on their syntactic structure. Clients must ensure that the resulting declaration sets are properly validated and processed.
Precondition
The input node n must be a valid non-null pointer to an SgNode object. The AST subtree rooted at n must be properly constructed and well-formed.
Postcondition
The returned DeclarationSets object contains all SgDeclarationStatement nodes found in the AST subtree. If no declarations are found, the function returns nullptr.
Note
This function uses a preorder traversal strategy to visit each node in the tree, which means that parent nodes are visited before their children. This allows clients to process declarations in the correct order and avoid potential issues with forward references or other dependencies between declarations.

◆ call_liveness_analysis()

LivenessAnalysis * SageInterface::call_liveness_analysis ( SgProject *  project,
bool  debug = false 
)

Performs liveness analysis on a given SgProject.

This function performs liveness analysis on the input SgProject using the DefUseAnalysis class. It first checks if the analysis has already been performed, and if so, returns the cached result. Otherwise, it creates a new instance of LivenessAnalysis, runs the def-use analysis, and then performs liveness analysis on each function body in the project.

Parameters
projectThe SgProject to perform liveness analysis on. Must not be NULL.
debugIf true, enables debugging output. Defaults to false.
Returns
A pointer to the LivenessAnalysis instance containing the results of the analysis. Returns NULL if an error occurs during analysis.
Warning
The function may abort and exit the program if an error occurs during analysis.
Precondition
The input project must not be NULL.
Postcondition
The returned LivenessAnalysis instance will contain the results of the analysis. 
  If an error occurs during analysis, the function will abort and exit the program.
Note
This function uses a recursive algorithm to perform liveness analysis on each function body. It also caches the result of the analysis to avoid redundant computation.

◆ changeBreakStatementsToGotos()

void SageInterface::changeBreakStatementsToGotos ( SgStatement *  loopOrSwitch)

Replaces break statements with goto statements in a given loop or switch statement.

This function takes a loop or switch statement as input and replaces all its break statements with equivalent goto statements. It does this by first identifying the body of the loop or switch statement, then finding all the break statements within that body. For each break statement found, it creates a new label statement and inserts it after the loop or switch statement, then replaces the break statement with a goto statement pointing to the newly created label.

The function uses a recursive approach to traverse the abstract syntax tree (AST) of the input code and identify the relevant statements.

Parameters
loopOrSwitchA pointer to an SgStatement representing the loop or switch statement in which to replace break statements with goto statements. Must be non-NULL and point to a valid loop or switch statement.
Returns
None (void function)
Warning
This function modifies the input code by replacing break statements with goto statements. The original break statements are lost in this process.
Precondition
The input loopOrSwitch must be non-NULL and point to a valid loop or switch statement.
Postcondition
All break statements within the body of the input loop or switch statement have been replaced with equivalent goto statements.
Note
This function uses a static counter to generate unique label names for the newly created labels. This means that the function is not thread-safe and should not be used concurrently by multiple threads.

◆ checkAccessPermissions()

SageInterface::checkAccessPermissions ( SgNode *  astNode)

Checks the access permissions of all defining and non-defining declarations in an Abstract Syntax Tree (AST) subtree.

This function traverses an AST subtree rooted at the given node, checking the access permissions of each declaration encountered. It outputs information about the access modifiers used in these declarations.

The traversal is performed using a preorder strategy, which visits the current node before recursively visiting its child nodes.

Parameters
astNodeThe root node of the AST subtree to be traversed. This node should represent the topmost declaration or statement in the subtree.
Returns
None. This function does not return any value; it simply outputs information about access modifiers used in declarations.
Warning
This function assumes that the input AST subtree is well-formed and contains valid declarations. If the input tree is malformed, this function may produce incorrect or misleading output.
Precondition
The input AST subtree should be non-empty and contain at least one declaration. The traversal strategy used (preorder) ensures that all child nodes of a given node are visited before their parent node is processed again.
Postcondition
After executing this function, the access modifier information for each declaration in the input AST subtree will have been output to the console. 
  No modifications are made to the original AST tree; this function only outputs information about existing declarations.
Note
This function uses a custom traversal class (DeclarationTraversal) that inherits from AstSimpleProcessing. The DeclarationTraversal class provides a customized visit() method for handling declaration nodes in the AST tree.

The traversal is performed in pre-order, meaning that for each internal node, the function first visits the node itself and then recursively traverses its child nodes.

Parameters
nodeThe root of the AST to be traversed. Must not be NULL.

Postcondition
The returned set contains all SgLocatedNodes that were marked as modified during the traversal of the input AST.
Note
This function uses a custom AstSimpleProcessing class, LocatedNodeTraversal, to perform the actual node traversal and collection. This allows for efficient handling of large ASTs.

Collects read-only variables from a given statement.

This function analyzes the given statement and collects the names of variables that are only read but not written. It uses two approaches: (1) precise analysis by collecting read-write variables using collectReadWriteVariables() and then computing the difference between read and write sets, or (2) a simple type-based approach if the first one fails.

readOnlyVarsA set of SgInitializedName pointers that will store the names of read-only variables found in the given statement.

Returns
None
Warning
If collectReadWriteVariables() fails, a simple type-based approach may not find all read-only variables.
Precondition
stmt must not be NULL.
Postcondition
readOnlyVars will contain the names of read-only variables found in the given statement.
Note
The function uses two approaches to collect read-only variables: precise analysis and simple type-based analysis. If the first approach fails, the second one is used as a fallback.

◆ deepDelete()

void SageInterface::deepDelete ( SgNode *  root)

Recursively deletes an abstract syntax tree (AST) rooted at the given node.

This function performs the following steps:

  1. Checks if the input statement is a SgBasicBlock, in which case no relocation of preprocessing information is done.
  2. Finds any attached comments and/or CPP directives to the target statement.
  3. If such comments/CPP directives exist and autoRelocatePreprocessingInfo is true, relocates them by finding a surrounding statement in the same file (looking up then down in the sequence of statements in this block) and moving the comments/CPP directives to that statement.
  4. Resets internal data structures that have references to the target statement (e.g., macro expansions).
  5. Removes the target statement from its parent statement or SgGlobal.
Note
This function is not supported within Microsoft Windows due to unknown reasons.

This function traverses the AST in post-order and deletes each node, ensuring that all child nodes are deleted before their parents to prevent memory leaks.

The actual deletion is performed by either a Visitor class or the deleteAST function, depending on the compilation configuration.

Parameters
rootThe root node of the AST to be deleted. Must not be NULL.
Returns
None
Warning
Deleting an AST can lead to undefined behavior if any pointers to nodes within the tree are still being used after deletion.
Precondition
The input parameter 'root' must point to a valid SgNode object that is part of an AST.
Postcondition
The entire AST rooted at 'root' has been deleted, and all memory allocated for its nodes has been freed.
Note
This function does not perform any error checking on the input parameter. It assumes that the caller has ensured the validity and correctness of the input data.

Finds the enclosing loop statement for a given statement in an Abstract Syntax Tree (AST).

This function traverses up the AST from a given statement to find the first enclosing loop statement. A loop statement is defined as any of the following: SgDoWhileStmt, SgForStatement, SgFortranDo, SgFortranNonblockedDo, or SgWhileStmt. If the label parameter is not empty, it will only consider loop statements with a matching label. The stopOnSwitches parameter determines whether to stop at switch statements.

Parameters
sThe statement from which to start searching for an enclosing loop statement. Must be non-null and valid in the AST.
labelA string representing a Fortran or Java label that must match the label of the enclosing loop statement. If empty, will consider any loop statement.
stopOnSwitchesA boolean indicating whether to return immediately when encountering a switch statement.
Returns
The first enclosing loop statement found in the AST, or NULL if none is found.
Warning
This function does not handle cycles in the AST. It assumes that the input statement is part of a valid AST.
Precondition
s must be non-null and valid in the AST.
Postcondition
If an enclosing loop statement is found, it will be returned; otherwise, NULL will be returned.
Note
This function uses a recursive approach to traverse up the AST. It may overflow the stack if the input statement is deeply nested in the AST.

◆ findUnusedLabels()

std::set< SgLabelStatement * > SageInterface::findUnusedLabels ( SgNode *  top)

Finds and returns a set of unused labels in the given AST.

This function traverses the Abstract Syntax Tree (AST) rooted at the specified SgNode* 'top' to identify all labels that are not referenced by any goto statements. It uses a custom visitor class, FindUsedAndAllLabelsVisitor, which inherits from AstSimpleProcessing and overrides its visit() method.

The function first initializes two sets: one for used labels (i.e., those referenced by goto statements) and another for all labels encountered during the traversal. It then traverses the AST in preorder, visiting each node to determine whether it's a goto statement or a label statement. If it's a goto statement, its target label is added to the set of used labels; if it's a label statement, it's added to the set of all labels.

After traversal, the function iterates over the set of used labels and removes each corresponding label from the set of all labels. The remaining labels in this set are considered unused.

Parameters
topThe root node of the AST to be traversed for finding unused labels.

string SageInterface::generateUniqueNameForUseAsIdentifier ( SgDeclarationStatement *  declaration)

Generates a unique name for use as an identifier.

This function generates a unique name that can be used as an identifier, typically for a variable or function. It uses the local node to name map and local name to node map maintained by the SageInterface class to ensure uniqueness.

The function first checks if the input declaration is already in the local node to name map. If it is, the corresponding unique name is returned. Otherwise, it tries to find a defining declaration for the input declaration and uses that to generate a unique name. If no defining declaration can be found, it uses the first non-defining declaration instead.

Parameters
declarationThe SgDeclarationStatement object for which a unique name is to be generated. Must not be NULL.
Returns
A string representing the unique name generated for the input declaration.
Warning
If the declaring declaration cannot be found in the local node to name map, this function will use the first non-defining declaration instead. This may lead to unexpected behavior if the non-defining declaration is not a valid identifier.
Precondition
The input declaration must not be NULL and must have been previously inserted into the local node to name map or have a defining declaration that has been inserted.
Postcondition
A unique name will be generated for the input declaration, which can then be used as an identifier.
Note
This function is not thread-safe, as it relies on the state of the SageInterface class.

◆ getDeclarationOfNamedFunction()

SgFunctionDeclaration * SageInterface::getDeclarationOfNamedFunction ( SgExpression *  func)

Retrieves the declaration of a named function from a given expression.

This function takes an expression as input and attempts to extract the declaration of a named function. It supports various types of expressions, including function references, dot operations, and arrow operations.

The function first checks if the input expression is a function reference. If so, it directly returns the declaration of the referenced function.

If the input expression is not a function reference, the function checks if it is a dot or arrow operation. In this case, it extracts the right-hand side operand and checks if it is a member function reference. If so, it returns the declaration of the referenced member function.

If none of the above conditions are met, the function issues a warning message to the standard error stream indicating that the input expression does not represent a named function.

Parameters
funcThe input expression from which to extract the declaration of a named function.
Returns
A pointer to the declaration of the named function if found; otherwise, NULL.
Warning
If the right-hand side operand of a dot or arrow operation is not a member function reference, a warning message is issued to the standard error stream.
Precondition
The input expression must be non-NULL.
Postcondition
If the function returns a non-NULL pointer, it points to a valid declaration of a named function.
Note
This function does not perform any semantic analysis on the input expression. It only checks the syntactic structure of the expression to determine if it represents a named function.

The function takes as input the loop statement, its corresponding node in the control flow graph, and references to two sets that will store the live-in and live-out variables. It returns no value but modifies the input sets accordingly.

Parameters
livA pointer to a LivenessAnalysis object that provides liveness information for the program.
loopA pointer to the SgForStatement representing the loop in the abstract syntax tree.
liveInsA reference to a set of SgInitializedName pointers that will store the live-in variables for the loop.
liveOutsA reference to a set of SgInitializedName pointers that will store the live-out variables for the loop.
Returns
None
Warning
This function assumes that the input loop statement is valid and has been correctly analyzed by the LivenessAnalysis class. If the loop statement is not valid or has not been properly analyzed, the results may be incorrect or undefined.
Precondition
The input loop statement must be a valid SgForStatement node in the abstract syntax tree. The LivenessAnalysis object must have been correctly initialized and provide accurate liveness information for the program.
Postcondition
The liveIns set will contain the variables that are live at the entry point of the loop, and the liveOuts set will contain the variables that are live at the exit point of the loop. These sets may be empty if no variables are live at these points.
Note
This function uses a recursive algorithm to traverse the control flow graph and compute the live-in and live-out sets for the loop. It assumes that the LivenessAnalysis class provides accurate liveness information for the program, which is used to determine the live variables at each point in the control flow graph.

Empty function or ill-formed function detected.

Retrieves a mangled name from a cache based on an Abstract Syntax Tree (AST) node.

This function attempts to retrieve a precomputed mangled name for the given AST node from a cache. The cache is stored in a map that associates AST nodes with their corresponding mangled names. If the mangled name is found in the cache, it is returned immediately; otherwise, an empty string is returned.

Parameters
astNodeThe Abstract Syntax Tree (AST) node for which to retrieve the mangled name. Must be a valid pointer to an SgNode object.

Precondition
The global scope of the AST node must be accessible to retrieve the mangled name cache.
Postcondition
If the mangled name is found in the cache, it is returned; otherwise, an empty string is returned.
Note
This function uses a recursive approach to find the global scope if it cannot be determined from the input AST node directly. It traverses up the AST hierarchy until it finds a valid global scope or reaches the root of the tree.

SgProject * SageInterface::getProject ( )

Retrieves the project node from the abstract syntax tree.

This function returns a pointer to the project node in the AST. The project node is the root of the AST and represents the entire source code file.

The implementation uses a traversal mechanism to visit nodes in the AST until it encounters an SgProject node, which is then returned as the result.

Parameters
None
Returns
A pointer to the project node in the AST. Returns NULL if no project node can be found.

If multiple project nodes are encountered during traversal, only the first one is returned. This may lead to unexpected behavior if the AST contains multiple project nodes.

The Abstract Syntax Tree (AST) must have been constructed prior to calling this function.

The returned project node pointer remains valid until the AST is modified or destroyed.

Note
This function uses a traversal mechanism, which may incur performance overhead for large ASTs.

◆ getSgNodeFromAbstractHandleString()

**brief Converts a reference to an initializable name **This function takes a node in abstract the syntax or NULL if it cannot be resolved *SgNode * SageInterface::getSgNodeFromAbstractHandleString ( const std::string &  input_string)

Retrieves an SgNode from a given abstract handle string.

This function is used to convert a reference to an initializable name in the abstract syntax tree (AST). It recursively traverses the AST to resolve the reference. The coarseGrain parameter determines whether to use coarse-grained or fine-grained conversion.

In general, this function is used in the context of static analysis, where it is necessary to convert references to initializable names in order to perform further analysis. Here are some examples of how this function can be used:

  • Converting a reference to an initializable name in a function call: SgFunctionCallExp* func_call = isSgFunctionCallExp(current); return convertRefToInitializedName(func_call->get_function(), coarseGrain);
  • Converting a reference to an initializable name in a class object: SgClassObject* obj = isSgClassObject(current); return convertRefToInitializedName(obj->get_class_name(), coarseGrain);

This function takes an abstract handle string as input and returns the corresponding SgNode if found. It uses the AbstractHandle class to build an abstract handle from the project and then creates another abstract handle using the trimmed input string. If the node is found, it is returned; otherwise, NULL is returned.

Parameters
input_stringThe abstract handle string used to retrieve the SgNode.
Returns
A pointer to the SgNode if found, or NULL otherwise.
Warning
This function may abort the program if AbstractHandle support is disabled for ROSE_USE_INTERNAL_FRONTEND_DEVELOPMENT.
Precondition
The input_string must be a valid abstract handle string.
Postcondition
If the node is found, it will be returned; otherwise, NULL will be returned.
Note
This function uses the AbstractHandle class to build and manipulate abstract handles. It also uses the SgNode class to represent the retrieved node.

The function uses a switch statement to check the variant type of the input scope. If the variant type matches one of the cases for simple children lists, the function returns true. ◆ instrumentEndOfFunction()

int SageInterface::instrumentEndOfFunction ( SgFunctionDeclaration *  func,
SgStatement *  s 
)

Instruments the end of a function by inserting statements before return statements.

This function instruments the end of a given function by inserting statements before each return statement. If no return statements are found, it appends the statements to the end of the function body.

The function first queries the function declaration for all return statements, then iterates over them to insert the given statement before each one. If a return statement has an expression that needs rewriting, it splits the expression before inserting the statement. It also avoids reusing the same statement by copying it.

Parameters
funcThe SgFunctionDeclaration representing the function to instrument. Must not be NULL and must have a valid definition.
sThe SgStatement to insert before each return statement or at the end of the function body if no return statements are found. Must not be NULL.
Returns
The number of times the statement was inserted.
Warning
If the function declaration is empty or ill-formed, this function will abort.
Precondition
The input function declaration and statement must not be NULL.
Postcondition
The function body has been modified to include the given statement before each return statement or at the end of the function body if no return statements are found.
Note
This function assumes that the input function declaration has a valid definition. If the function body is empty, it will abort.

◆ isInSubTree()

SageInterface::isInSubTree ( SgExpression *  subtree,
SgExpression *  exp 
)

Checks if an expression is contained within a given subtree.

This function traverses the abstract syntax tree (AST) of the given subtree and checks if the specified expression is present within it. It utilizes a visitor pattern to perform the traversal efficiently.

The function uses a recursive approach to explore the AST, ensuring that all nodes are examined thoroughly. If the target expression is found during the traversal, the function immediately returns true; otherwise, it returns false.

Parameters
subtreeThe root node of the subtree to search within.
expThe target expression to search for within the subtree.
Returns
True if the target expression is found within the subtree; false otherwise.
Warning
This function assumes that the provided subtree and expression are valid and non-null. Failure to meet these preconditions may result in undefined behavior or crashes.
Precondition
The input subtree and expression must be valid, non-null pointers.
Postcondition
The function will not modify the input subtree or expression.
Note
This function has a time complexity of O(n), where n is the number of nodes in the subtree. It is designed to be efficient for large ASTs.

◆ isOverloaded()

SageInterface::isOverloaded ( SgFunctionDeclaration *  functionDeclaration)

Checks if a given function declaration is overloaded.

This function checks for any other function that might overload the input function. For member functions, it only looks in the scope where the member function is defined. For non-member functions, it looks only in the scope where the function is declared. Note that there are scenarios where this approach of searching only these locations might not catch an overloaded function. See notes below for details.

Parameters
functionDeclarationThe input function declaration to be checked for overloading.
Returns
True if the function is overloaded, false otherwise.
Warning
This function may not detect all cases of overloaded functions due to its limited search scope. For member functions, it does not check base classes or friend functions in other classes. For non-member functions, it does not check different namespace definitions or friend functions in classes.
Precondition
The input function declaration is valid and not null.
Postcondition
None
Note
This function uses a counter to detect overloaded functions. If more than one function with the same name is found, it returns true, indicating that the function is overloaded.
For member functions, this function checks if there are other member functions with the same name in the same class. It does not check base classes or friend functions in other classes.
For non-member functions, this function checks if there are other non-member functions with the same name in the same scope. It does not check different namespace definitions or friend functions in classes.

◆ isPrototypeInScope()

bool SageInterface::isPrototypeInScope ( SgScopeStatement *  scope,
SgFunctionDeclaration *  functionDeclaration,
SgDeclarationStatement *  startingAtDeclaration 
)

Checks if a prototype of a given template member function declaration is already present in the specified scope.

This function searches for an existing previously inserted (or existing) template member function declaration within the provided scope and returns true if found, indicating that there's no need to add another one. The search starts from the specified startingAtDeclaration position in the scope's declaration list.

Parameters
scopeThe SgScopeStatement object representing the scope where the prototype is to be searched for.
functionDeclarationThe SgFunctionDeclaration object representing the template member function declaration to be searched for.
startingAtDeclarationThe SgDeclarationStatement object representing the position in the scope's declaration list from which the search should start.
Returns
True if a prototype of the given template member function declaration is already present in the specified scope, false otherwise.
Warning
This function assumes that the input parameters are valid and not null. It does not perform any error checking on them.
Precondition
The scope parameter must be non-null and represent a valid SgScopeStatement object.
The functionDeclaration parameter must be non-null and represent a valid SgFunctionDeclaration object.
The startingAtDeclaration parameter must be non-null and represent a valid SgDeclarationStatement object.
Postcondition
If the function returns true, it means that a prototype of the given template member function declaration is already present in the specified scope, and there's no need to add another one. If the function returns false, it means that no such prototype was found, and a new one can be added if needed.
Note
This function uses the get_declarationList() method of SgScopeStatement class which is only properly defined for certain scopes.
The search performed by this function starts from the specified startingAtDeclaration position in the scope's declaration list and proceeds linearly until the end of the list. If a match is found, the loop exits early to optimize performance.

*endcode *bool SageInterface::isUseByAddressVariableRef ( SgVarRefExp *  ref)

Checks if a variable reference is used by address in an expression.

This function determines whether the given variable reference is being used as an operand for the unary '&' operator, or as a parameter of a function call where the corresponding parameter has a reference type. It checks two main cases: (1) if the parent node of the variable reference is an SgAddressofOp node, indicating that it's being used as an operand for the unary '&' operator; and (2) if the parent node is an SgExprListExp, indicating a function call, in which case it checks whether the parameter type at the corresponding index has a reference type.

Parameters
refThe variable reference to check. Must not be NULL.
Returns
True if the variable reference is used by address in the expression; false otherwise.
Warning
This function assumes that the input SgVarRefExp node is valid and points to a non-NULL parent node. Failure to meet this precondition may result in undefined behavior.
Precondition
The input SgVarRefExp node must not be NULL, and its parent node must also not be NULL.
Postcondition
The function will return true if the variable reference is used by address; otherwise, it returns false.
Note
This function does not handle cases where there are type casting operations between the variable reference and its parent node. It also assumes that the SgFunctionCallExp node has a valid SgFunctionRefExp child node.

◆ lastFrontEndSpecificStatement()

SgStatement * SageInterface::lastFrontEndSpecificStatement ( SgGlobal *  globalScope)

Retrieves the last frontend-specific statement in a global scope.

This function iterates over the declarations in a given global scope and returns the last statement that is frontend-specific. A frontend-specific statement is one whose file information indicates that it was generated by the frontend.

The purpose of this function is to provide a way for clients to determine where to insert new statements into a global scope, particularly when inserting at the top of the scope.

Parameters
globalScopeThe global scope in which to find the last frontend-specific statement. Must not be NULL.
Returns
A pointer to the last frontend-specific statement in the given global scope, or NULL if no such statement exists. If an error occurs, a fatal assertion will be triggered.
Warning
The function assumes that the input global scope is valid and has at least one declaration.
Precondition
The globalScope parameter must not be NULL.
Postcondition
The returned pointer will either point to a frontend-specific statement or be NULL.
Note
This function uses an iterator to traverse the declarations in the global scope, which may involve iterating over a large number of statements. Clients should use this function judiciously and only when necessary.

◆ lookupNamespaceSymbolInParentScopes()

SgNamespaceSymbol * SageInterface::lookupNamespaceSymbolInParentScopes ( const SgName &  name,
SgScopeStatement *  cscope = NULL 
)

Looks up a namespace symbol in the parent scopes.

This function searches for a namespace symbol with the given name in the current scope and its parent scopes. It returns the first matching symbol found in the search order.

The search order is as follows:

  1. Current scope: The function checks if the symbol exists in the current scope. If it does, the function returns the symbol immediately.
  2. Parent scopes: If the symbol is not found in the current scope, the function moves to the parent scope and repeats the search process until a match is found or there are no more parent scopes.
Parameters
nameThe name of the namespace symbol to look up.
cscopeThe current scope where the search starts. If NULL, the topmost scope in the scope stack is used as the starting point.
Returns
A pointer to the namespace symbol if found; otherwise, returns NULL.
Warning
If the input scope (cscope) is NULL, the function uses the topmost scope in the scope stack as the starting point. This may lead to unexpected results if the scope stack is modified concurrently.
Precondition
The input name must be a valid SgName object.
Postcondition
If a matching symbol is found, the returned pointer remains valid until the symbol is removed from its containing scope or the program terminates.
Note
This function uses a recursive approach to search for the symbol in the parent scopes. It may cause stack overflow if the scope hierarchy is too deep.

◆ loopInterchange()

bool SageInterface::loopInterchange ( SgForStatement *  loop,
size_t  depth,
size_t  lexicoOrder 
)

Interchanges loops in a loop nest based on a given lexicographical order.

This function reorders the loops in a loop nest according to a specified lexicographical order. The input loop must have at least two levels and the lexicographical order must be less than the factorial of the depth of the loop nest. The function first verifies the input parameters, then saves the headers of the loops in the nest, converts the lexicographical number to a permutation order array, and finally rewrites the loop nest based on this permutation.

Parameters
loopThe SgForStatement representing the loop nest to be interchanged. Must not be NULL.
depthThe size_t representing the depth of the loop nest. Must be greater than 1.
lexicoOrderThe size_t representing the lexicographical order of the permutation. Must be less than the factorial of the depth and not equal to 0.
Returns
True if the interchange is successful, false otherwise.
Warning
This function may modify the input loop nest and its children loops.
Precondition
The input loop must have at least two levels and the lexicographical order must be less than the factorial of the depth of the loop nest.
Postcondition
The loop nest is modified according to the specified permutation.
Note
This function assumes that the input loop has n perfectly-nested children loops inside, where n is the depth of the loop nest.

targetLevelThe level at which to perform tiling.

True if the operation is successful, false otherwise.

◆ moveStatementsBetweenBlocks() [2/4]

Moves statements between blocks in the abstract syntax tree.

This function relocates statements from a source block to a target block in the abstract syntax tree. It is used to reorganize the structure of the code and ensure that declarations are properly nested within scopes.

The function first moves declarations between scopes using the moveDeclarationsBetweenScopes helper function. Then, it creates alias symbols for global definitions by calling createAliasSymbols on the parent node of the target block, which is expected to be an SgNamespaceDeclarationStatement.

Moves a file to a subdirectory in the project.

This function transforms the abstract syntax tree (AST) by inserting a new SgDirectory node between the given SgFile and its parent. It updates the parents and file lists accordingly, effectively moving the file to the specified subdirectory when unparsed.

The transformation is done in three steps:

  1. A new SgDirectory node is created with the given directory name.
  2. The SgDirectory node is inserted between the SgFile and its parent (either an SgProject or another SgDirectory).
  3. The file is moved to the new subdirectory by updating the parents and file lists.

None
Warning
This function modifies the AST, which may affect the behavior of other functions that operate on the same AST.
Precondition
The given SgFile node must exist in the project and have a valid parent (either an SgProject or another SgDirectory).
Postcondition
The file is moved to the specified subdirectory, and the parents and file lists are updated accordingly.
Note
This function uses the ROSE_ASSERT macro to ensure that the preconditions are met. If the assertions fail, it indicates a programming error.

Normalizes a for-loop initialization declaration by separating variable declarations from the loop condition.

This function transforms a for-loop with an initialization declaration into a standard form where the variable declaration is moved outside of the loop and only the assignment part remains in the loop. For example, it converts "for (int i = 0; ...)" to "int i; for (i = 0; ...)". This transformation helps to improve code readability and maintainability.

loopThe input SgForStatement node representing the for-loop that needs normalization. It must not be NULL. If it is, a ROSE_ASSERT will fail.

True if the normalization was successful, false otherwise. A return value of true means the function has modified the input AST (Abstract Syntax Tree). The original variable declaration statement is replaced with an assignment statement and a new variable declaration statement is prepended to the enclosing function's body.

Precondition
The input SgForStatement node must be valid and non-NULL. The function has write access to the input AST.
Postcondition
If true is returned, the input AST has been modified. A new variable declaration statement has been prepended to the enclosing function's body. The original variable declaration statement in the loop initialization has been replaced with an assignment statement.
Note
This normalization does not handle cases where the loop initialization contains complex declarations such as Decomposition::Iterator ditr(&decomp). Such loops are considered non-canonical and this normalization will not be applied to them.

◆ normalizeForLoopTest()

*endcode *bool SageInterface::normalizeForLoopTest ( SgForStatement *  loop)

Normalizes the test expression of a for loop.

This function normalizes the test expression of a given for loop by transforming certain binary operations into their equivalent forms. The normalization is done to facilitate further analysis or transformation of the loop.

The function checks if the test expression is a binary operation and, if so, applies the following transformations:

  • Less-than (<) operations are transformed into less-or-equal (<=) operations by subtracting 1 from the right operand.
  • Greater-than (>) operations are transformed into greater-or-equal (>=) operations by adding 1 to the right operand.

If the test expression is not a binary operation or if it cannot be normalized, the function returns false. Otherwise, it returns true.

Parameters
loopThe for loop whose test expression is to be normalized. Must be non-null and have a valid test expression.
Returns
True if the test expression was successfully normalized, false otherwise.
Warning
This function modifies the input loop's test expression. If the original expression needs to be preserved, a copy of the loop should be made before calling this function.
Precondition
The input loop is non-null and has a valid test expression.
Postcondition
The input loop's test expression has been normalized if possible.
Note
This function does not handle all possible binary operations. It only handles less-than, greater-than, less-or-equal, and greater-or-equal operations.

◆ ReductionRecognition()

void SageInterface::ReductionRecognition ( SgForStatement *  loop,
std::set< std::pair< SgInitializedName *, OmpSupport::omp_construct_enum > > &  results 
)

Recognizes reduction patterns in a for loop.

This function analyzes the given for loop to identify variables that are used as reductions. A reduction is recognized when a variable is assigned a value based on its previous value, typically using an operator such as '+', '*', 'min', or 'max'. The function returns a set of pairs containing the identified reduction variables and their corresponding OpenMP construct types.

Parameters
loopThe for loop to analyze for reductions.
resultsA set to store the recognized reduction variables and their corresponding OpenMP construct types.
Returns
None. The results are stored in the 'results' parameter.
Warning
This function assumes that the input loop is a canonical for loop, i.e., it has an initializer, a condition, and an incrementor. If the loop does not meet this assumption, the function may produce incorrect results or crash.
Precondition
The input loop must be a valid SgForStatement node in the ROSE AST.
Postcondition
The 'results' set contains all recognized reduction variables and their corresponding OpenMP construct types.
Note
This function uses various heuristics to recognize reductions, including:
  • Variables referenced at most twice within the loop body.
  • Assignments to a variable based on its previous value using an operator.
  • If statements that assign a value to a variable based on its previous value.

◆ reset_name_collision_map()

void SageInterface::reset_name_collision_map ( )

Resets the name collision maps to their initial state.

This function clears all data structures used for tracking name collisions, effectively resetting them to their initial empty state. It is typically called when a new compilation unit or scope is entered, ensuring that any previously recorded name collisions are discarded and do not affect the processing of the new code segment.

The function implements an O(1) operation as it simply clears three maps: local_name_collision_map, local_name_to_node_map, and local_node_to_name_map, without performing any additional computations or checks.

Parameters
None.This function does not take any parameters.
Returns
None. This function does not return a value.
Warning
The caller is responsible for ensuring that this function is called in the correct context, as resetting these maps prematurely can lead to incorrect results or errors during further processing.

None. There are no preconditions for calling this function.

All name collision maps have been reset to their initial state.

Note
This function is part of the internal implementation of SageInterface and should not be called directly from external code without careful consideration of its implications on the overall processing workflow.

◆ resetInternalMapsForTargetStatement()

SageInterface::resetInternalMapsForTargetStatement ( SgStatement *  sourceStatement)

Resets internal maps for a target statement by updating data structures that hold references to the statement.

This function allows the modification of the input statement to trigger operations on internal data structures that hold references to such statements. An example is the macro expansion data structures that have a reference to the statements that are associated with and macro expansion. If a statement associated with a macro expansion is removed, then the macro expansion needs to be updated to force all of the statements to be marked as transformed (so that the AST will be unparsed instead of the tokens representing the macro or some partial representation of the transformed statements and the macro call).

Parameters
sourceStatementThe statement for which internal maps need to be reset. Must not be NULL. If the statement has not yet been added to the AST, it will not return a valid pointer.
Returns
None
Warning
This function does not check if the input statement is valid or if it has already been processed. It assumes that the input statement is valid and needs to be processed.
Precondition
The input statement must be a valid SgStatement object.
Postcondition
Internal maps are updated to reflect changes to the input statement.
Note
This function updates data structures such as macroExpansionMap, representativeWhitespaceStatementMap, and redundantlyMappedTokensToStatementMultimap. It also marks statements in the macro expansion as transformed and sets them to be output in code generation.

◆ scopeHasStatementsFromSameFile()

bool SageInterface::scopeHasStatementsFromSameFile ( SgScopeStatement *  scope)

Checks if a given scope contains statements from the same file.

This function determines whether a scope has any statements that must be unparsed because they originate from the same file as the scope. It supports token-based unparsing when used with header files and helps identify when a statement from a header file may contain a transformation that requires individual unparsing of statements.

Parameters
scopeThe SgScopeStatement object to check for statements from the same file. Must not be NULL. If the scope is empty or contains only declarations, it will return false unless a statement with the same file ID is found.
Returns
True if there is at least one statement in the scope that has to be unparsed (i.e., originates from the same file as the scope), false otherwise. If the scope contains only declarations or no statements, it will return false.
Warning
This function assumes that the input SgScopeStatement object is valid and not NULL. Passing an invalid or NULL pointer may result in undefined behavior.
Precondition
The input SgScopeStatement object must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to a scope.
Postcondition
If the function returns true, it guarantees that there is at least one statement in the scope with the same file ID as the scope. If it returns false, it does not guarantee the absence of such statements but indicates that none were found.
Note
This function uses a recursive approach to check each statement in the scope. It first checks if the scope contains only declarations and then iterates over the declaration list or statement list accordingly. If it finds a statement with the same file ID as the scope, it immediately returns true.

Sets the stride of a loop in the abstract syntax tree (AST) to the given expression.

This function updates the increment statement of a for/do loop with the provided stride expression. It supports various forms of increment statements and handles different types of loops.

The supported forms of increment statements include:

  • i++ or i– (post-increment/decrement)
  • i+=X or i-=X (addition/subtraction assignment)
  • i=i+X or i=X+i (addition)
  • i=i-X or i=X-i (subtraction)

The function also handles Fortran DO loops and updates their increment statements accordingly.

Parameters
loopA pointer to the SgNode representing the loop in the AST. Must not be NULL.
strideA pointer to the SgExpression representing the new stride value. Must not be NULL.
Returns
None

If the loop is not a for/do loop or a Fortran DO loop, an error message is printed and the function asserts false.

Precondition
The input loop and stride must be valid and non-NULL.
Postcondition
The increment statement of the loop is updated with the new stride expression.

◆ setOperand()

void SageInterface::setOperand ( SgExpression *  target,
SgExpression *  operand 
)

Sets the operand of a given expression.

This function sets the operand of a given expression to a new value. It handles different types of expressions and updates their operands accordingly.

The function takes two parameters: the target expression whose operand is to be set, and the new operand expression. It first checks if both parameters are valid, then uses a switch statement to handle different types of expressions.

For each type of expression, it calls the corresponding setter method to update the operand. If the expression type is not handled by the switch statement, it checks if the expression is a unary operation and updates its operand accordingly. If none of these cases match, it prints an error message and aborts.

Finally, the function sets the parent of the new operand to the target expression and marks the left-hand side values of the target expression.

Parameters
targetThe target expression whose operand is to be set. Must not be NULL.
operandThe new operand expression. Must not be NULL and must not be the same as the target expression.
Returns
None
Warning
If the target expression is not one of the handled types, an error message will be printed and the program will abort.
Precondition
The target expression and the operand expression must not be NULL. The target expression and the operand expression must not be the same.
Postcondition
The operand of the target expression will be updated to the new value.
Note
This function assumes that the target expression and the operand expression are valid and have been properly initialized.

This function determines the source position classification mode and sets the source position of the given SgNode accordingly. The source position classification mode can be one of several predefined values, including e_sourcePositionDefault, e_sourcePositionTransformation, e_sourcePositionCompilerGenerated, e_sourcePositionNullPointers, or e_sourcePositionFrontendConstruction.

Depending on the mode, this function may set the source position to a default value, classify it as a transformation, mark it as compiler-generated code, set pointers to Sg_File_Info objects to NULL, or specify it to be filled in during AST construction in the front-end.

None

Precondition
The input node must not be NULL.
Postcondition
The source position of the input node has been set according to the current SourcePositionClassification mode.
Note
The behavior of this function depends on the current SourcePositionClassification mode, which can be changed using the getSourcePositionClassificationMode() and setSourcePositionClassificationMode() functions.

void SageInterface::setStatic ( SgDeclarationStatement *  stmt)

Sets the static storage modifier for a declaration statement.

This function modifies a given SgDeclarationStatement by setting its storage modifier to static. The static keyword in C++ is used to specify internal linkage, which means that the variable or function can only be accessed from within the same translation unit where it was defined.

Parameters
stmtA pointer to an SgDeclarationStatement for which the static storage modifier will be set. Must not be NULL.
Returns
None
Warning
This function does not perform any checks on whether the input statement is a valid candidate for setting the static storage modifier. It is up to the caller to ensure that the statement can have its storage modifier set to static without causing undefined behavior.
Precondition
The input SgDeclarationStatement must be non-NULL and have a valid declaration modifier.
Postcondition
The storage modifier of the input SgDeclarationStatement will be set to static.
Note
This function does not return any value, but instead modifies the input statement in-place. It is up to the caller to ensure that this modification has the desired effect on the program's behavior.

◆ suggestNextNumericLabel()

int SageInterface::suggestNextNumericLabel ( SgFunctionDefinition *  func_def)

Suggests a numeric label value for a Fortran 77 function.

This function scans the symbol table of the given function definition to find the maximum numeric label value used and suggests a new label value by adding 10 to the maximum found. The suggested label is ensured to be within the valid range for Fortran 77 labels (i.e., not exceeding 5 digits).

Parameters
func_defA pointer to an SgFunctionDefinition object representing the function for which a numeric label value is to be suggested. Must not be NULL. The function must also be in Fortran language.
Returns
A suggested numeric label value, at least 10 greater than the maximum existing label value found in the function's symbol table.
Warning
If no labels are found in the function's symbol table, a default value of 10 is returned.
Precondition
The input SgFunctionDefinition object must not be NULL and must represent a Fortran language function.
Postcondition
The returned label value will be at least 10 greater than any existing label value in the function's symbol table.
Note
This function assumes that the input function definition is valid and has been parsed correctly.

◆ translateScopeToUseCppDeclarations()

SageInterface::translateScopeToUseCppDeclarations ( SgScopeStatement *  scope)

Translates a given scope to use C++ declarations.

This function processes the statements in the provided SgScopeStatement and translates them to use C++ declarations. It handles both declaration-only scopes (e.g., global scope, namespace definitions, class definitions) and scopes that contain non-declaration statements (e.g., SgBasicBlock). The translation process involves attaching preprocessor directives to the statements in the scope.

Parameters
scopeThe SgScopeStatement to be translated. Must not be NULL.
Returns
None.
Warning
This function modifies the input scope by inserting preprocessor directives. It also removes attached preprocessing information from the statements.
Precondition
The input scope must be a valid SgScopeStatement.
Postcondition
The input scope is modified to use C++ declarations. Attached preprocessing information is removed from the statements in the scope.
Note
This function uses a recursive approach to process the statements in the scope. It also relies on the skipTranslateToUseCppDeclaration() function to determine which directives should be skipped during translation.

Translates a given statement to use C++ declarations.

Parameters
statementThe input statement to be translated.
scopeStatementThe scope statement associated with the input statement.
Returns
A vector of SgC_PreprocessorDirectiveStatement pointers representing the translated directives.
Warning
This function assumes that the input statement has attached preprocessing information. If not, an empty vector will be returned.

◆ translateToUseCppDeclarations()

void SageInterface::translateToUseCppDeclarations ( SgNode *  n)

Translates a given SgNode to use C++ declarations.

This function traverses the Abstract Syntax Tree (AST) subtree rooted at the given SgNode and translates it to use C++ declarations. It uses a recursive algorithm implemented through the CppTranslationTraversal class, which is an AstSimpleProcessing subclass. The traversal visits each node in the AST, checks if it's a scope statement, and if so, processes it using the translateScopeToUseCppDeclarations function.

Parameters
nThe SgNode representing the root of the AST subtree to be translated. Must not be NULL.
Returns
None. This function does not return any value.
Warning
This function modifies the AST in-place and may cause unintended side effects if not used carefully.
Precondition
The input SgNode must represent a valid AST subtree.
Postcondition
The AST subtree rooted at the input SgNode is modified to use C++ declarations.
Note
This function uses a postorder traversal, meaning that it visits the child nodes before their parent node. This is done to ensure that all necessary transformations are applied to the child nodes before they are visited by the parent node.

Postcondition

Note

◆ wrapAllTemplateInstantiationsInAssociatedNamespaces()

void SageInterface::wrapAllTemplateInstantiationsInAssociatedNamespaces ( SgProject *  root)

Wraps all template instantiations in their associated namespaces.

This function traverses the Abstract Syntax Tree (AST) of a given SgProject and identifies all template instantiations. It then moves each instantiation into its associated namespace, effectively wrapping it.

The function uses a recursive approach to traverse the AST, checking each node for template instantiations. If an instantiation is found, it is added to a vector of SgDeclarationStatement pointers. After traversing the entire AST, the function then iterates over this vector and moves each declaration into its associated namespace.

Parameters
rootThe root node of the SgProject's Abstract Syntax Tree (AST).
Returns
None
Warning
This function modifies the input AST by moving template instantiations into their associated namespaces. Use with caution.
Precondition
The input SgProject must be valid and have a properly constructed AST.
Postcondition
All template instantiations in the input SgProject's AST will be wrapped in their associated namespaces.
Note
This function is not available when using CMake due to limitations in the current implementation. It is only available when using autotools.
